name: model-preferences-routing
title: Model Preferences Routing
purpose: TUI for managing orchestrator/worker model routing in OpenCode. Users define named mappings pairing an orchestrator model with a worker model, then activate a mapping to apply it globally across all agents and commands.

requirements.title: Role Classification
requirements.body: The system must classify every target (agent or command) as either 'orchestrator' or 'worker' based on its kind and mode. Commands always map to orchestrator. Agents with mode 'subagent' map to worker; all others (primary, all, empty) map to orchestrator.

scenarios.title: Primary agent is orchestrator
then: returns RoleOrchestrator

scenarios.title: Subagent is worker
then: returns RoleWorker

scenarios.title: All-mode agent is orchestrator
given: an agent with mode 'all' or empty mode
then: returns RoleOrchestrator

scenarios.title: Command is always orchestrator
then: returns RoleOrchestrator regardless of mode field

requirements.title: Routing Config in Separate File
requirements.body: Routing configuration (named mappings) must be stored in a separate file (~/.config/opencode/omp-routing.json), NOT in opencode.json. This is required because opencode.json uses additionalProperties:false and rejects unknown keys. The path must respect OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR.

scenarios.title: Routing path respects OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR
given: OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR is set to a custom directory
then: returns {OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR}/omp-routing.json

scenarios.title: Missing file returns empty config
then: returns empty RoutingConfig with no error

scenarios.title: Writes are atomic
then: writes to a temp file then renames
no temp files remain after success

requirements.title: Mapping CRUD
requirements.body: The system must support creating, reading, updating, and deleting named mappings. Each mapping has a name, an orchestrator model ID, and a worker model ID. Mappings are persisted in omp-routing.json.

scenarios.title: Create a new mapping
scenarios.when: a mapping is created via the TUI form
then: the mapping is appended to the mappings list
the routing config is saved to disk

scenarios.title: Edit an existing mapping
scenarios.when: the user edits 'fast' via the TUI form
then: the mapping is updated in-place
the routing config is saved to disk

scenarios.title: Delete a mapping
then: the mapping is removed from the list
the routing config is saved to disk

requirements.title: Apply Active Mapping
requirements.body: Activating a mapping writes the orchestrator model to all primary/all agents and commands, and the worker model to all subagents, in opencode.json. Uses sjson chaining for a single atomic file operation. Only writes to agents/commands that already have an entry in opencode.json (does not create new entries).

scenarios.title: Orchestrator model applied to primary agents
given: agents build and plan with mode primary exist in config
then: agent.build.model and agent.plan.model are set to 'anthropic/claude-opus-4'

scenarios.title: Worker model applied to subagents
given: agents general and explore with mode subagent exist in config
then: agent.general.model and agent.explore.model are set to 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4'

scenarios.title: Commands get orchestrator model
then: command.deploy.model is set to 'anthropic/claude-opus-4'

scenarios.title: Activation warns about existing preferences
given: agents already have model preferences set
then: a warning is shown listing affected agents
a second 'a' press is required to confirm

scenarios.title: Only writes to existing config entries
given: a target exists in discovery but has no entry in opencode.json
then: no new agent/command entry is created in opencode.json

requirements.title: Mapping List View
requirements.body: The TUI must display a list of saved mappings with section headers. Each mapping shows its name, orchestrator model, and worker model. A '(+ new mapping)' entry allows creating new mappings. The list supports filtering.

scenarios.title: Empty state shows new mapping entry
then: the list shows an Actions section with '(+ new mapping)'

scenarios.title: Mappings appear with details
then: the list shows 'quality' with orchestrator and worker model IDs

requirements.title: Mapping Editor with huh
requirements.body: Creating or editing a mapping uses a charmbracelet/huh form with fields for name, orchestrator model (select from discovered models), and worker model (select from discovered models).

scenarios.title: Form shows discovered models
given: models are discovered from CLI or config
scenarios.when: the user opens the mapping editor
then: orchestrator and worker selects show all discovered model IDs

scenarios.title: Edit pre-fills existing values
then: name, orchestrator, and worker fields are pre-filled with current values

requirements.title: Dual-File Persistence
requirements.body: The system uses two config files: opencode.json for agent/command model assignments (written by ApplyActiveMapping), and omp-routing.json for routing mappings (written by SaveRouting). Writes to opencode.json use tidwall/sjson for surgical JSON path updates that preserve formatting. Writes to omp-routing.json use atomic temp+rename.

scenarios.title: sjson preserves formatting
then: existing structure is preserved
only model fields are updated

scenarios.title: Routing config is separate from opencode.json
then: mappings are written to omp-routing.json, not opencode.json

requirements.title: Model Discovery
requirements.body: Models are discovered using a CLI-first strategy: run 'opencode models' to get the live model list, falling back to parsing provider.*.models from opencode.json if the CLI fails or returns empty. On startup, 'opencode models --refresh' is called to update the provider registry.

scenarios.title: CLI models used when available
given: opencode models returns a list of models
then: CLI models are used, not config models

scenarios.title: Falls back to config when CLI fails
given: opencode models fails or returns empty
then: models are parsed from provider.*.models in opencode.json

scenarios.title: Refresh runs on startup
then: opencode models --refresh is called before loading config

requirements.title: Agent Filtering
requirements.body: System agents (compaction, title, summary) must be excluded from target discovery. All other agents (built-in user-facing and user-defined) must be included. Agents are categorized by mode for role classification.

scenarios.title: System agents excluded
given: config has agents: build, plan, compaction, title, summary
then: build and plan are included
compaction, title, and summary are excluded

scenarios.title: Agents categorized by mode
then: build is classified as orchestrator
explore is classified as worker

requirements.title: Target Discovery
requirements.body: The system discovers targets from three sources: built-in agents (build, plan as primary/locked; general, explore as subagent), markdown agent/command files (global + project directories), and JSON-configured agents/commands in opencode.json. Markdown mode wins over JSON default. Hidden agents are tracked but may be filtered in display.

scenarios.title: Built-in agents always present
then: build, plan, general, explore are present

scenarios.title: Markdown mode wins over JSON default
given: a markdown agent with mode: subagent
a JSON entry for the same agent with no mode
then: the agent's mode is 'subagent' (from markdown, not 'all' from JSON default)

scenarios.title: Project agents discovered from .opencode directory
given: a .opencode/agents/ directory exists in the project tree
then: markdown agents from the project directory are included

requirements.title: Mapping Validation
requirements.body: When creating or editing a mapping, the system warns (does not block) if the orchestrator or worker model ID is not found in the discovered model list. Validation is advisory since models may be available at runtime but not at config time.

scenarios.title: Valid models produce no warnings
given: both orchestrator and worker models exist in the discovered list
then: returns empty warnings

scenarios.title: Unknown model produces advisory warning
given: the orchestrator model is not in the discovered list
then: returns a warning string mentioning the unknown model
does not return an error

requirements.title: User Role Taxonomy
requirements.body: The system declares five named user roles (brain, tasker, builder, librarian, fixer) as vocabulary for future model assignment. These roles are declarative only — not yet wired to routing or target-mapping logic. They are exported so callers can reference them in UI and documentation.

scenarios.title: All five roles declared
then: returns exactly 5 roles: brain, tasker, builder, librarian, fixer

scenarios.title: Each role has a description
then: returns a non-empty description string

scenarios.title: User roles do not affect routing
scenarios.when: RoleForTarget is called on any target
then: classification is unchanged — still based on Kind/Mode, not UserRole
